cards.title: NCA Clearance and Volume Definitions (CL, CL/F, Vss, Vz)
cards.claim: Total body clearance (CL) is calculated as Dose/AUCINF for IV dosing. For extravascular dosing, apparent clearance (CL/F) is used because F cannot be estimated. Volume of distribution at steady state (Vss) is computed as MRTINF * CL (or CLss) and is NOT computed for extravascular dosing because MRTINF includes mean input time. Volume of distribution based on terminal phase (Vz) is Dose/[Lambda_z * AUCINF]; for extravascular dosing, this is effectively Vz/F. Lambda_z is estimated by linear regression of log concentration (Y) on time (X).
conditions: Vss is only valid for IV Bolus and Infusion models.
For infusion models, MRTINF = (AUMCINF/AUCINF) - (Tinf/2). Do not subtract Tinf/2 again when calculating Vss.
For extravascular models (e.g., oral), parameters are apparent (CL/F, Vz/F).
Lambda_z estimation requires sufficient points in the terminal log-linear phase.
limitations: Vss cannot be calculated for extravascular data using standard NCA formulas due to absorption phase influence on MRT.
CL/F and Vz/F are not true physiological parameters but apparent values dependent on F.
NCA parameters assume linear kinetics unless specified otherwise; they do not describe time-varying clearance.
cards.downstream_use: Use CL/CL/F for exposure-response analysis and dose adjustment. Use Vss for understanding tissue distribution extent in IV studies. Use Vz for terminal half-life interpretation. Do not mix apparent and absolute parameters in the same model without explicit F assumptions.
cards.retrieval_keywords: CL, CL/F, Vss, Vz and Vc definitions and conditions
